title: Marigold Telecom rate-limit playbook (draft)
content:
Context:
- Marigold Telecom (edge/mobile MVNO) exploring Redwood Private in their EU + APAC regions. Primary ask: predictable per-tenant throughput and strict rate limiting per customer account.
- Initial POC scope: chat assistant for customer support (multilingual), fallback to hosted API if capacity saturates, and tight billing visibility by customer and route.

Call summary (2025-02-14):
- Attendees: Marigold: Lina Cortez (CTO), Rakesh Iyer (Platform), Anya Petrov (SRE); Redwood: Elena Park (SE lead), Samir P. (Eng), Greta N. (SRE advisor)
- Lina opened with business constraints: must avoid noisy neighbors, want hard caps per tenant (not just soft quotas). Need spike protection during campaign blasts.
- Rakesh emphasized ops constraints: limited public IPs, will use private deployment behind their NAT; they require KMS integration for key custody and audit logs for all inference requests.
- SLOs: target median latency <= 120ms for chat up to 128 tokens; p95 <= 300ms. Throughput target: 60 concurrent sessions per region, peak 250 QPS across model calls during campaigns.
- Security: GDPR + telecom-regs in EU, need VPC peering and encrypted logs; no traffic can leave EU region for EU customers.

Key requirements (explicit):
1) Per-tenant hard rate limiting (token-level and request-level) enforced at the edge-gateway in Private deployment.
2) Token-bucket policy per account with burst window and steady-state limits; ability to define override policies for support agents.
3) Fallback policy config: when dedicated pool is saturated, route to a lower-cost hosted model with opt-in by customer. Must log fallback events per request.
4) Billing/export: daily per-customer token and request CSVs + per-route cost attribution.
5) KMS/HSM integration for model keys; rotate every 90 days and provide key-usage audit.
6) Latency SLO monitoring with alerting on p95 breach by 10% (auto-create ticket).
7) Fine-grained role-based access for their ops + support teams.

Technical gotchas noted during discussion:
- Rate limiting location: doing hard enforcement inside customer VPC means local enforcement but complicates cross-region quotas. If they want a global cap across EU+APAC, we need a central control plane signal (latency for updates must be measured).
- Token counting semantics: Marigold wants billing to align with their existing unit (characters per language). Need mapping from Redwood token counts to their billing units; provide a conversion table and sample data for first 1000 sessions.
- Hot-cache warm-up: customer workflows include long form context injection at session start (user profile + previous tickets ~3–4k tokens). If we evict prefix caches during scale-up, cold starts will blow p95. Recommend pre-warming KV cache for new session templates (see action item).
- Burst scenarios: marketing campaigns create sudden spikes of ephemeral sessions. Continuous batching helps throughput but can add tail latency; propose conservative batching settings with dynamic thresholds tied to observed p95.

Architecture proposals (options to present in POC):
A) Local enforcement + periodic control-plane sync (preferred for strict isolation): enforce per-tenant hard limits in Private edge; periodic (1s–10s) token counters synced to control plane for billing and global caps. Tradeoff: eventual consistency for cross-region caps.
B) Centralized enforcement proxy (control-plane mediates all rate decisions): stronger global guarantees but single point of failure and requires cross-region routing of control messages—may not meet their data residency needs.
C) Hybrid: local hard caps for region-level usage + control-plane aggregated counters for global billing and campaign throttles.

Recommended POC config (what Elena/SE propose):
- Start with option C. Rationale: respects EU residency while giving Marigold visibility and ability to set global campaign-level throttles.
- Rate-limit policy example (initial): per-tenant steady: 20 qps, burst: 100 qps for 10s window, token cap: 200k tokens/minute. Admin override role for support with separate token bucket.
- Batching: set continuous batching max batch latency 15ms, max batch size tuned in POC to maintain p95 budget.
- Cache strategy: pre-warm KV caches for top 10 session templates; maintain 10% reserved cache memory per instance to avoid full eviction on burst.

Open questions to clarify (for next call):
- Lina: do they require cross-region hard caps (global hard limit) or is per-region hard cap acceptable?
- Rakesh: exact KMS vendor + access method (HSM provided by cloud provider or on-prem HSM?). Need integration docs and expected SLA for key calls.
- Anya: SRE wants exact alerting thresholds and escalation path for p95 breaches—do they want automatic failover to hosted or manual?
- Billing mapping: need sample of 30 days of historical traffic (anonymized) to build conversion table and cost model.

Action items (owners & tentative dates):
- SE: produce a short POC design doc with option C details + sequence diagram (Elena) — due 2025-02-21.
- Eng infra: prototype local token-bucket enforcement module for Private (Samir) — demo w/ simple CLI by 2025-03-04.
- SRE consultant: draft alert/playbook for p95 breaches and automated fallback criteria (Greta) — due 2025-02-25.
- Marigold: provide 30 days anonymized traffic sample and KMS vendor details (Lina/Rakesh) — target 2025-02-20.
- Billing: create token->billing-unit conversion prototype and cost projection for 3 scenarios (low, expected, high) (Jonah) — due 2025-02-27.

Notes / working thoughts:
- For the POC, instrument every fallback event with request metadata (tenant, reason, latency, model variant) to feed Redwood Optimize later for quantization/variant recommendations.
- Consider implementing a lightweight webhook that pushes per-tenant counters every 10s to Marigold’s billing collector for reconciliation.

Risks identified:
- If they require global hard caps with zero tolerance for eventual consistency, Private deployment alone might not suffice without a central enforcement plane (which conflicts with data residency). Need legal/ops to sign off if we surface any EU->control-plane traffic.
- KMS latency could add to p95 if key unwrap occurs per-request; recommend caching decrypted keys within HSM constraints and rotate on schedule rather than per-request.

Next steps (near term):
1) Share this note and the POC design stub with Marigold and ask for the anonymized traffic file + KMS details (Elena, today).
2) Internal sync with infra + SRE to align on prototype constraints and dependencies (Samir + Greta, 2025-02-18).
3) Schedule follow-up with Marigold to review POC config and sample outputs (tentative 2025-02-24).

Misc scratchpad (short reminders):
- Demo plan: show stuck sessions / cache warm vs cold difference, fallback audit log, per-tenant CSV export.
- Quick test data: create synthetic campaign spike with 5x base QPS for 2 minutes to validate burst policies.
- Keep capture of any regulatory red flags and surface to security-compliance team early.

---
End of notes.
